summary:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based Mars outpost survival simulator engineered to teach students (ages 8–14), educators, and space enthusiasts how real astronauts make life-critical engineering trade-offs in deep space.
The project is built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. It uses the browser's built-in Web Audio API to procedurally synthesize retro-futuristic sound effects with zero external audio downloads, an interactive HTML5 3D Canvas for Martian landing site navigation, and a dual-tier storage engine powered by Neon Serverless Postgres with automatic local failover.
details:
Project Overview: What It Does & How It Works

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based Martian survival and mission-command simulation designed for students ages 8–14. Players take on the role of a Mars habitat commander tasked with surviving a 30-sol mission by balancing four interconnected life-support systems: Power, Oxygen, Radiation Shielding, and Crew Morale.

Before launching, players spin an interactive 3D Martian Globe to choose between three authentic NASA landing zones, Jezero Crater (Perseverance site), Gale Crater (Curiosity site), or Olympus Mons Caldera, each applying real environmental modifiers to solar efficiency, atmospheric density, and radiation exposure. Each sol, players execute operational actions (such as running Oxygen generators, repairing solar arrays, or conducting research) while responding to real-time crises driven by live and historical NASA datasets. Throughout the mission, a Live NASA DONKI Space Weather Ticker streams real solar flare and Coronal Mass Ejection (CME) alerts, while a real-time Telemetry Analytics Console plots multi-series resource curves and hazard markers across all 30 sols.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Traditional STEM education often teaches space science through passive worksheets where facts are memorized in isolation. Our goal is to replace passive memorization with systems thinking and active decision-making:

Cause-and-Effect Literacy: Kids immediately experience how environmental trade-offs work, for example, why high-altitude solar arrays at Olympus Mons generate more power while thinner atmosphere increases oxygen and radiation strain.

Accessible STEM Engagement: Between sols, bite-sized NASA STEM facts and a curated Mars Rover Photo Gallery (Perseverance, Curiosity, Opportunity, Spirit) connect gameplay directly to real planetary exploration.

Replayability & Progression: Three difficulty tiers (Space Cadet, Mission Commander, and Mars Pioneer), four crew specialties, unlockable mission badges, a server-validated global leaderboard, and a printable completion certificate encourage sustained learning and classroom competition.

Technologies, Tools & NASA Data Used

Frontend & Visualization: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, custom HTML5 <canvas> 3D sphere rendering for the interactive Mars globe, zero-dependency responsive SVG telemetry sparklines, and Web Audio API procedural sound synthesis (zero external audio files required).

Backend & Cloud Persistence: Next.js Route Handlers, Neon Serverless PostgreSQL (@neondatabase/serverless) for multi-cadet profiles, cloud save resumption, and anti-cheat score verification, deployed on Vercel.

NASA & Partner Data Sources:

NASA DONKI (/api/nasa-live + local cache): Live and historical solar flare (FLR) and CME telemetry dynamically scales crisis severity and radiation penalties, backed by an automatic offline failover cache.

NASA OSDR (Space Biology): Peer-reviewed spaceflight studies (OSD-253, OSD-352, OSD-412, etc.) power in-game scientific discoveries and link directly to primary research.

NASA OSDR / CSA ISS RadLab: Real absorbed radiation dose-rate spikes, calibrate radiation shielding drain during solar storms.

NASA Mars Rover Photos & Mars Trek: Authentic rover surface photography and topographic coordinates power the Rover Gallery and landing site selector.

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

Child-First UX & Safety (COPPA/GDPR-Minded): Young players use auto-generated space callsigns rather than personal emails or passwords, and a two-step Delete Account control permanently erases all local and Neon Postgres cloud records on demand.

Resilient Hybrid Architecture: Recognizing that classrooms and live events can have unstable internet connections, the live NASA DONKI telemetry pipeline includes a 3.5-second timeout with seamless fallback to curated local NASA datasets, and the Rover Gallery features built-in SVG telemetry fallbacks so the experience never breaks offline.

Fair, Transparent Math: Rather than relying on opaque randomness, every action displays exact resource trade-offs upfront, empowering students to calculate their own survival strategies.
